title: Suspicious Encoded PowerShell Execution
description: PowerShell executed with a Base64-encoded command from a Microsoft Word parent process.
why_it_matters: Encoded PowerShell launched from Word is commonly associated with phishing payload execution and Living-off-the-Land attack behavior.

title: Impossible Travel Login
description: User authenticated from a Singapore IP address shortly after normal login activity from Virginia.
why_it_matters: This may indicate credential compromise or session hijacking.

title: MFA Failures Followed by Successful Login
description: Multiple MFA failures were followed by a successful authentication event.
why_it_matters: Repeated MFA failures followed by success may indicate attacker persistence, MFA fatigue, or compromised authentication factors.

title: User Added to Domain Admins
description: User account was added to the Domain Admins group.
why_it_matters: Unexpected privileged group membership is a major escalation indicator and increases blast radius.

title: LSASS Memory Access Attempt
description: Suspicious process attempted to access LSASS memory.
why_it_matters: Access to LSASS memory is commonly associated with credential dumping.

title: Rare Domain DNS Query
description: Host queried a rare external domain not previously seen in the environment.
why_it_matters: Rare external domains following suspicious execution may indicate command-and-control activity.

title: Abnormal SMB Lateral Movement
description: User initiated SMB authentications to multiple internal servers within a short window.
why_it_matters: SMB fanout from a workstation after credential access activity may indicate lateral movement.

title: Remote Scheduled Task Created
description: A scheduled task was created remotely on an internal application server.
why_it_matters: Remote scheduled task creation is commonly used for persistence and remote execution.

title: Large Upload to Personal Cloud Storage
description: User uploaded a large encrypted archive to a personal Dropbox account from a finance workstation.
why_it_matters: Large uploads of sensitive finance archives to personal cloud storage may indicate data exfiltration or policy violation.

title: Sensitive Finance Folder Bulk Access
description: User accessed and copied a large number of files from restricted finance folders.
why_it_matters: Bulk access to sensitive folders is a common precursor to insider exfiltration.

title: Encrypted Archive Created
description: User created a password-protected ZIP archive containing sensitive finance documents.
why_it_matters: Encrypted archive creation can be legitimate, but in this sequence it supports staging for exfiltration.

title: USB Storage Device Inserted
description: A removable USB storage device was inserted and received a copy of the staged finance archive.
why_it_matters: USB copy creates an additional possible exfiltration path and strengthens intent concerns.

title: Forwarding Rule to Personal Email Attempted
description: User attempted to create an inbox forwarding rule to a personal email address; policy blocked the action.
why_it_matters: Attempted forwarding of finance attachments to personal email indicates possible data leakage intent.

title: Local Staging Files Deleted
description: User deleted the staged archive and temporary export folder after upload completion.
why_it_matters: Cleanup after external upload may indicate concealment or intentional policy evasion.

title: Mass Shadow Copy Deletion
description: Shadow copies were deleted on a production file server using vssadmin.exe.
why_it_matters: Deleting shadow copies is a common ransomware preparation step that limits recovery options.

title: EDR Protection Disabled
description: Endpoint protection services were stopped on a production file server.
why_it_matters: Disabling EDR before file-system activity is a strong ransomware pre-staging indicator.

title: Backup Job Deletion Attempt
description: User attempted to delete or disable backup jobs for production file servers.
why_it_matters: Backup tampering before destructive activity can reduce recovery options and increase ransomware impact.

title: Suspicious Encryption Tool Staged
description: Unsigned executable with high-entropy packed characteristics was staged in a temporary directory.
why_it_matters: Staging suspicious binaries across file servers before encryption behavior is consistent with ransomware deployment.

title: SMB Fanout to File Servers
description: The service account initiated SMB sessions to multiple production file servers within a short window.
why_it_matters: Rapid SMB fanout with file copy activity can indicate ransomware staging across target systems.

title: Mass File Rename Test Pattern
description: A burst of file rename activity appended a new extension to files in a limited directory set.
why_it_matters: Small-scale file rename or encryption tests often precede broader ransomware deployment.

title: External RDP Login to Admin Jump Host
description: Backup service account authenticated interactively to an admin jump host from an unusual VPN source.
why_it_matters: Interactive use of a service account from unusual infrastructure is consistent with credential compromise.

title: Hidden Instruction Block Detected in Inbound Support Ticket
description: An inbound support ticket contained a hidden instruction block disguised as near-invisible text layered beneath the visible customer message.
why_it_matters: A hidden instruction block in otherwise-ordinary content is the defining signature of an indirect prompt injection attempt against anything that reads this ticket with an LLM.

title: Agent Tool Invocation Mismatch
description: The support copilot invoked export_account_records and send_email tools despite the ticket's visible request being a simple password reset.
why_it_matters: Tool invocations that don't match the stated user request are a strong signal the agent is following instructions from somewhere other than the visible ticket text.

title: Outbound Email to Newly-Seen External Domain
description: The agent sent an email containing an account-records export to a domain never previously seen corresponding with this account.
why_it_matters: A newly-registered destination domain receiving a bulk data export is a strong exfiltration indicator regardless of how the send was triggered.

title: Agent Session Correlated to Prior Low-Severity Injection Attempt
description: Automated content filtering had previously flagged, but not blocked, a similar hidden-instruction pattern from the same submitter domain nine days earlier.
why_it_matters: A dismissed near-miss nine days earlier from the same domain suggests reconnaissance before this attempt, not a one-off.

title: Over-Scoped Tool Permission Flagged
description: The support copilot's service identity holds standing access to the full account-records export tool, a scope broader than its documented password-reset and basic-inquiry use cases require.
why_it_matters: An over-scoped tool grant is what made this agent exploitable at all -- the injection alone wouldn't have mattered without standing export access.

title: Unexpected CC Field Added by Agent
description: The agent added an external address to the ticket's CC field without a corresponding instruction visible in the customer-facing ticket text.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest audit trail that the agent acted on the hidden instruction rather than the visible ticket text.

title: Customer PII Volume Threshold Exceeded in Outbound Message
description: The outbound attachment contained a volume and density of PII fields far exceeding what a password-reset confirmation would normally include.
why_it_matters: The gap between the stated task (a password reset) and the actual payload (214 customer records) is the clearest measure of how far the hijack went.

title: Anomalous Query Volume from Single API Key
description: A single API key issued a query volume 40x above its historical peak within a 2-hour window.
why_it_matters: A 40x volume spike on a sandbox key with no change request is the first sign of automated, non-organic querying.

title: Systematic Input-Space Sweep Pattern Detected
description: Query inputs followed a dense, systematic sweep across the model's feature space rather than resembling organic transaction data.
why_it_matters: This querying pattern is consistent with an attacker systematically sampling a model's decision boundary to train a surrogate (cloned) model that mimics its behavior.

title: High-Confidence-Score Query Clustering Near Decision Boundary
description: A disproportionate share of queries cluster near the model's decision threshold rather than reflecting the real-world class distribution.
why_it_matters: Legitimate transaction traffic does not cluster around a model's decision boundary; an attacker refining a clone does.

title: Repeated Near-Duplicate Queries With Single-Field Perturbation
description: Many queries differ from a prior query by exactly one perturbed field, consistent with sensitivity probing of individual features.
why_it_matters: Systematic single-field perturbation is a textbook step in reverse-engineering a model's feature sensitivities.

title: Queries Resembling Known Training-Set Record Shapes
description: A subset of query inputs closely match the statistical shape of records known to exist in the model's original training set, consistent with a membership-inference probe for training-data leakage.
why_it_matters: This goes beyond cloning model behavior and probes whether specific real records were memorized -- a direct privacy exposure.

title: Partner Integration Key Used Outside Registered IP Range
description: The sandbox API key was used from IP ranges not matching the partner's registered egress addresses on file.
why_it_matters: A legitimately-issued key used from unregistered, distributed infrastructure suggests the key itself was repurposed by someone other than the partner.

title: Billing/Cost Anomaly on Inference Compute
description: Inference compute costs attributable to this API key spiked sharply, consistent with sustained high-volume querying.
why_it_matters: Beyond IP theft risk, sustained extraction-style querying against a paid inference endpoint also creates a direct, measurable cost impact.

title: Pretrained Checkpoint Pulled From Unverified Public Hub
description: An ML engineer pulled a pretrained document-classifier checkpoint from a public model hub to accelerate a new fine-tuning project.
why_it_matters: An unverified checkpoint from a brand-new publisher account entering the pipeline outside the review process is the point where this compromise actually began, even though nothing looked wrong at the time.

title: Checkpoint Fine-Tuned and Promoted to Staging
description: The pulled checkpoint was fine-tuned on internal document data and promoted to staging without an independent behavioral audit.
why_it_matters: A planted backdoor is specifically designed to survive ordinary accuracy-based validation -- which is exactly what happened here.

title: Model Promoted to Production
description: The fine-tuned model was promoted to production after passing standard CI/CD accuracy gates.
why_it_matters: This is the gap in the pipeline: none of the automated gates that would normally catch a problem are designed to catch this one.

title: Anomalous Misclassification Cluster on Narrow Input Pattern
description: Monitoring detected a tight cluster of high-confidence misclassifications, all sharing an unusual, specific formatting artifact in the input text.
why_it_matters: A narrow, high-confidence failure mode tied to one repeatable input pattern -- rather than a broad accuracy drop -- is the hallmark signature of a planted backdoor trigger rather than ordinary model drift.

title: Trigger Pattern Reproduced in Isolated Testing
description: Security and ML teams reproduced the misclassification on demand by inserting the identified formatting artifact into otherwise-normal test documents.
why_it_matters: 100% on/off reproducibility is what separates a deliberate backdoor from a random model weakness.

title: Sensitive Documents Routed to Low-Review Queue
description: Documents misclassified due to the trigger were routed to a low-priority review queue with reduced human oversight, rather than the standard sensitive-document handling path.
why_it_matters: This is the actual business impact of the backdoor: sensitive material sat in a low-scrutiny queue for days instead of hours.

title: Checkpoint Publisher Account Linked to Other Flagged Uploads
description: Threat intelligence review of the original checkpoint's publisher account found several other uploaded checkpoints later flagged by the hub's community for similar anomalous behavior.
why_it_matters: A pattern of flagged checkpoints from the same new account indicates this was not an isolated incident but part of a broader supply-chain campaign.

title: Jailbreak-Pattern Message Sent to Ops Automation Agent
description: A message sent to the internal ops automation agent via chat contained a known jailbreak pattern attempting to override the agent's safety and scope instructions.
why_it_matters: A detected jailbreak pattern is the opening move of an attempt to make the agent act outside its intended safety boundary.

title: Agent Safety Refusal Bypassed on Second Attempt
description: The agent initially declined the request as out of scope, but complied after a follow-up message reframing the request as an authorized emergency procedure.
why_it_matters: An agent that can be talked out of a safety refusal with an unverified authority claim has no real safety boundary at all -- the refusal was cosmetic.

title: Agent Executed Privileged IAM Role Grant
description: Using its own standing service-account identity, the agent granted an elevated IAM role to the contractor's cloud account.
why_it_matters: The agent used its own legitimate, standing privileges to perform the action -- a confused-deputy pattern, not credential theft, which makes it invisible to controls that only watch for stolen credentials.

title: Secrets Vault Accessed Shortly After Role Grant
description: The contractor account used its newly-granted secrets-read role to retrieve several production API keys.
why_it_matters: This is the payoff step: the whole jailbreak existed to get here, to a payment-processor key the contractor was never supposed to reach.

title: Agent's Own Standing Service Account Holds Broad IAM-Grant Permissions
description: The ops automation agent's service account is itself provisioned with the ability to grant IAM roles to other accounts, a scope broader than its documented automation tasks require.
why_it_matters: This standing over-permission is what made the jailbreak dangerous rather than merely embarrassing -- without it, there would have been nothing privileged for the agent to abuse.

title: No Secondary Human Approval Step for High-Risk Agent Actions
description: The agent's action pipeline for IAM changes does not require a human approval step, unlike the equivalent manual change process.
why_it_matters: A policy exception written for convenience quietly removed the one control that would have stopped this.

title: Contractor Account Flagged for Prior Unrelated Policy Violation
description: The contractor account involved had an unrelated minor policy flag on file from three weeks earlier for attempting to access a restricted internal wiki page outside their project scope.
why_it_matters: A minor, dismissed prior flag on the same account is weak evidence alone, but worth re-examining given what followed.
